standard: both halves (signal before / from 2024-01-01): > 0 after 0.8% and 1.2% cost, better than the average liquid stock bought and sold at the same moments (rule and yardstick capped at +300%, AUD-1), better than the same stock on its other days, > 0 without the 2 best, 20+ trades and 3+ blocks, block t >= 2.5 -> TRADABLE SMALL; block t >= 4.1 -> PROVEN

SQ6-CLENOW.name: Clenow "Stocks on the Move" momentum (weekly, regression slope x R2)
SQ6-CLENOW.who: Andreas Clenow (CIO of ACIES Asset Management; the book publishes the full rules and a 1999-2014 S&P 500 simulation)

sources.cite: Clenow (2015) Stocks on the Move: Beating the Market with Hedge Fund Momentum Strategies
QuantConnect forum: Andreas F. Clenow momentum (rules restated, 2018)

SQ6-CLENOW.rule: Weekly, on the first session of each week that falls on a Wednesday or later (his Wednesday). Universe: the 500 most traded liquid stocks (S&P 500 proxy). Score = annualised exponential regression slope of the last 90 closes (OLS of ln close on day number; exp(slope x 252) - 1) x the regression R2. Rank the universe; the top 20% (100) are the buy / keep zone. A stock may be held only if its close is above its 100-day average and it had no one-day move of 15%+ (close to close) in the last 90 sessions. SELL (next open) a held stock that leaves the top 20%, closes under its 100-day average, has a 15%+ move, or leaves the universe. BUY (next open), only when SPY closes above its 200-day average: from the top of the ranking down, stocks not held that pass the filters, each sized 0.1% of the account / ATR(20) (ATR as a fraction of the close; capped at 10% of the account), while the summed sizes fit in 100%; the first one that does not fit stops the buying.
SQ6-CLENOW.deviations: S&P 500 membership is proxied by the 500 most traded liquid stocks (no point-in-time index list); the every-other-week size rebalance is not modelled; each position is judged as one trade (equal weight per trade, the system standard), its size is recorded.

SQ6-RADGE.name: Radge Weekend Trend Trader (20-week high, ROC 30%+, index filter, 40%/10% trailing stop)
SQ6-RADGE.who: Nick Radge (The Chartist; published the rules with a long simulated and live record)

sources.cite: usethinkscript: Weekend Trend Trader by Nick Radge (rules restated from the book)

SQ6-RADGE.rule: Weekly, on the last session of each week. Liquid stock; this week's close is the highest weekly close of the last 20 weeks; 20-week rate of change (week close / week close 20 weeks earlier - 1) >= 30%; SPY's week close above the 10-week average of its week closes. BUY the next open. EXIT, checked on each week close (review levels, not live stops): stop = highest week close since entry x 0.60 while SPY's week close is above its 10-week average, x 0.90 when it is below; the stop only rises; a week close under the stop sells at the next open. At most 504 sessions (then the close).
SQ6-RADGE.deviations: The book trades a liquid index universe (Russell 1000 / ASX); here every liquid stock. "20-week high" read as a 20-week closing high.

SQ6-CRSIPB.name: Connors ConnorsRSI pullback (limit 4% under the close, out when ConnorsRSI > 50)
SQ6-CRSIPB.who: Larry Connors / Connors Research (published high-win-rate stock pullback system)

sources.cite: Connors Research, ConnorsRSI pullback system as published in Active Trader, March 2013 (rules as coded on Wealth-Lab)
Connors & Alvarez (2012) An Introduction to ConnorsRSI

SQ6-CRSIPB.rule: Daily. Close above 5 USD, 21-day average volume 250k+ shares (and the system's liquid floor); ADX(10) > 30; today's low at least 4% under yesterday's close; today's close in the bottom 25% of its range; ConnorsRSI(3,2,100) < 15. ConnorsRSI = (Wilder RSI(3) of the close + RSI(2) of the up/down streak + percent rank of today's 1-day return among the previous 100) / 3. BUY: a limit order for the next session at today's close x 0.96 (filled at the open if it opens under it). SELL: the next open after the first close with ConnorsRSI > 50. No stop (as published). At most 60 sessions (then the close). One open trade per stock.
SQ6-CRSIPB.deviations: The published exit sells AT the close; here the next open (the standard). Max 60 sessions is our cap (none published).

SQ6-CUMRSI.name: Connors cumulative RSI(2) on stocks over the 200-day (2-day sum < 35, out at RSI(2) > 65)

sources.cite: Connors & Alvarez (2008) Short Term Trading Strategies That Work, ch. "Cumulative RSI"

SQ6-CUMRSI.rule: Daily. Liquid; close above its 200-day average; Wilder RSI(2) of today + RSI(2) of yesterday < 35. BUY the next open. SELL the next open after the first close with RSI(2) > 65. No stop. At most 60 sessions. One open trade per stock.
SQ6-CUMRSI.deviations: Published for indices / ETFs with a buy at the close; applied to liquid stocks and bought at the next open. Differs from DEC2-RSI2 (RSI(2) < 5, out over the 5-day average) and A-SW1 (RSI(2) < 10, max 5 sessions).

SQ6-MTUM.name: MSCI USA Momentum index method (iShares MTUM): risk-adjusted 6 and 12-month momentum, semi-annual
SQ6-MTUM.who: MSCI index rulebook tracked by iShares MTUM (public methodology, live since 2013)

sources.cite: MSCI Momentum Indexes Methodology (May 2017; current edition 2025)

SQ6-MTUM.rule: At the close of the last session of May and of November. Universe: the 600 most traded liquid stocks with 252+ sessions of history (MSCI USA proxy). 12-month momentum = close 21 sessions ago / close 252 sessions ago - 1; 6-month = close 21 ago / close 126 ago - 1; each divided by the annualised standard deviation of weekly returns over up to 3 years (156 weeks, 52 at least); each turned into a z-score across the universe, averaged 50/50, standardised again and winsorised at +-3. BUY the next open the 120 stocks (20% of the universe) with the highest positive combined z-score. SELL at the close of session 126 (the next review).
SQ6-MTUM.deviations: Market-cap x score weighting, the 50% buffer and the ad-hoc rebalance are not modelled; equal weight per trade; no risk-free rate (it is common to every stock); the first reviews have under 3 years of weekly returns; the universe is a traded-value proxy.

SQ6-QMOM.name: Alpha Architect Quantitative Momentum (QMOM): top 10% 12-2 momentum, the smoother half, quarterly
SQ6-QMOM.who: Wes Gray & Jack Vogel (Alpha Architect; QMOM ETF live since Dec 2015, rules published in the book and fund documents)

sources.cite: Gray & Vogel (2016) Quantitative Momentum; Alpha Architect QM education deck

SQ6-QMOM.rule: At the close of the last session of February, May, August and November (their seasonal quarterly rebalance). Universe: the 1000 most traded liquid stocks with 252+ sessions, REITs (SIC 6798) left out. Momentum = close 21 sessions ago / close 252 sessions ago - 1 (2-12). Keep the top 10% (100). Frog-in-the-pan FIP = sign(momentum) x (% of down days - % of up days) over the same sessions; BUY the next open the 50 with the LOWEST FIP (smoothest), equal weight. SELL at the close of session 63.
SQ6-QMOM.deviations: No 25% sector cap, no high-beta screen, traded-value universe proxy; the fund went monthly in Q4 2024, the book's quarterly seasonal schedule is used throughout. Overlaps DEC-FROG (all liquid stocks, monthly, top 30% then 30 smoothest, hold 126): here large caps, quarterly, top 10% then 50, hold 63.

SQ6-3WT.name: O'Neil / IBD three-weeks-tight breakout (buy over the 3-week high, 8% stop, +20% target)
SQ6-3WT.who: William O'Neil / David Ryan (IBD; Ryan won the US Investing Championship with CAN SLIM; 3-weeks-tight is one of their add / buy points)

sources.cite: O'Neil, How to Make Money in Stocks (4th ed., 2009), three-weeks-tight; IBD rule restated in TradingView "3 Weeks Tight - CANSLIM Technical Indicator"

SQ6-3WT.rule: Weekly, on the last session of each week. Liquid; the last 3 week closes each within 1.5% of the week close before it (2 tight steps); a prior advance: the first of the 3 week closes is 20%+ above the lowest week close of the 12 weeks before it; close > 50-day > 200-day average; 126-session return in the top 30% of liquid stocks that day (RS 70+ proxy). BUY: a buy-stop at the highest daily high of the 3 weeks + 0.10 USD, valid the next 5 sessions. STOP 8% under the fill (intraday, O'Neil's 7-8% rule); TARGET +20% (intraday, his 20-25% profit rule); else the close of session 63. Stop and target the same day = stop. One open trade per stock.
SQ6-3WT.deviations: No EPS / composite rating (needs data); RS rating proxied by the 126-session return rank; the 8-week hold exception after a fast +20% is not modelled (DEC2-IBD has it).

SQ6-TD9.name: DeMark TD Sequential buy setup 9 (perfected), 1-4 bar bounce
SQ6-TD9.who: Tom DeMark (indicators licensed to Bloomberg / used by large funds; no public personal record)

sources.cite: DeMark (1994) The New Science of Technical Analysis, TD Sequential setup

SQ6-TD9.rule: Daily. Liquid; a completed TD buy setup: 9 closes in a row each lower than the close 4 sessions earlier, the close before bar 1 NOT lower than the close 4 sessions before it (bar 9 is today, not bar 10+); perfected: the lower of the lows of bars 8 and 9 <= the lower of the lows of bars 6 and 7. BUY the next open (skipped if it opens at or under the stop). STOP: the lowest low of the 9 setup bars (intraday). SELL at the close of the 4th session (the expected 1-4 bar reaction). One open trade per stock.
SQ6-TD9.deviations: DeMark gives no fixed exit; the 4-session exit and the setup-low stop are our reading of the 1-4 bar reaction and the TD risk level.
